purpose: Photographic evidence for the PHYSICAL layout of the Weltzeituhr drum. Each record is a dated photograph contributing layout constraints. Names alone are not the object; band and within-face order are.
contamination_note: Historical photographs are admissible object evidence. No claimed-K4-solution site used. See docs/contamination-log.md.
CRITICAL_GEOMETRY_RULE: The city cylinder is STATIC; the hour ring ROTATES. An hour numeral appearing beneath a face therefore does NOT identify that face's time zone. Identify a face from its CITY CONTENTS and physical adjacency only. A record may carry visible_hour_ring_values, but they must never be used to assign utc_sector.
transcription_rule: Every transcription carries transcription_status: LOCAL VISUAL EVIDENCE (this agent read the image pixels itself, in-session) or EXTERNAL-AGENT TRANSCRIPTION (a text handoff only). LOCAL VISUAL supersedes EXTERNAL-AGENT for the same face. Unclear letters/lines are UNKNOWN, never guessed.

ordering_analysis.question: Is within-band order alphabetical, geographic, or neither?

evidence_for_alphabetical.utc+1_upper_1970s: AMSTERDAM BERLIN BRUSSEL BUDAPEST MADRID PARIS PRAG STOCKHOLM WARSCHAU is in STRICT alphabetical order. P(random)=1/9!=2.76e-6.
evidence_for_alphabetical.multi_name_groups: All five reported multi-name groups across the 1984 and 1989 frames are alphabetical (ALMA-ATA/TASCHKENT, KRASNOJARSK/NOWOSIBIRSK, IRKUTSK/ULAN-BATOR, CHABAROWSK/WLADIWOSTOK, MAGADAN/SACHALIN). P(random)=2^-5=0.031.
evidence_for_alphabetical.discriminator: The SAME external agent transcribed the modern lower band (Source 7) as OSLO KOPENHAGEN WIEN BERN PRESSBURG BELGRAD ROM TUNIS KINSHASA, which is NOT alphabetical. So the agent does not alphabetise by habit, which argues the alphabetical readings are genuine physical order.

evidence_against_a_universal_rule.historical_lower_subset: KOPENHAGEN WIEN BELGRAD TUNIS is NOT alphabetical but IS strictly decreasing in latitude (55.7, 48.2, 44.8, 36.8).
evidence_against_a_universal_rule.modern_lower_band: OSLO KOPENHAGEN WIEN BERN PRESSBURG BELGRAD ROM TUNIS KINSHASA is latitude-ordered north-to-south with a single inversion (Bern before Pressburg), 1 of 8 adjacent comparisons against 18 expected at random.

ordering_analysis.current_reading: UPPER bands look ALPHABETICAL; LOWER bands look GEOGRAPHIC (north to south). Two different rules on one face is odd but is what the data shows.
ordering_analysis.why_it_matters: If a band's order is rule-determined, ORDER follows from MEMBERSHIP. That turns the acquisition requirement from 'a fully legible ordered transcription' into 'enough legibility to identify WHICH names are present' - a much weaker requirement.
ordering_analysis.grade: SUPPORTED, NOT PROVEN. Rests on one external agent and cannot be verified locally.
ordering_analysis.local_visual_update: Superseded in part. The upper band's alphabetical rule is now LOCAL VISUAL confirmed on the CET face. The lower band is confirmed NOT alphabetical, which the earlier analysis had left open.

date_problem.status: REVISED. The arithmetic gap that generated this problem is CLOSED; a sharper problem replaces it.

closed_part.resolution: The 1985 first major maintenance (Tagesspiegel, 14 Apr 2019, Erich John profile) is a third change boundary. 146 - 80 - 20 = 46 is exactly the quantity the 1985 event has to account for.
closed_part.grade: The arithmetic closes exactly, which is suggestive but is not itself proof that 1985 added 46 names; the source names only four (Athen, Kopenhagen, Wien, Rom).
closed_part.consequence: If the change boundaries are 1969, 1985 and 1997, then any frame datable to [1985, 1997) shows the 1988-89 target state. Dating becomes a yes/no question instead of an open-ended growth curve.

open_part.crux: UPLOAD-1 (the only frame with a fully transcribed face) is internally contradictory on date.
for_1985_or_later: ROM present - all three named as 1985 additions
for_before_1985: ATHEN, the fourth named 1985 addition, is NOT visible
for_before_1997: MOSKAU present - LOCAL VISUAL, independent of any caption
open_part.logic: Either the Tagesspiegel 1985 change set is wrong (or is a re-engraving of names already present, which would reconcile everything), or the WELT caption is wrong. A re-engraving reading is the cheapest reconciliation and would put the frame in the 1970s with those names already on the drum - in which case the frame still is not target-era evidence, only evidence of stability.
open_part.consequence: Tier 1 hinges entirely on dating this one image. No amount of further analysis of the pixels I have can settle it.

new_blocker_soviet_zones.statement: Historical ZONE MEMBERSHIP differs from modern, beyond the single documented Kiew move.
new_blocker_soviet_zones.evidence: The 1984 frame groups ALMA-ATA with TASCHKENT on one face. They sit in different modern zones (UTC+6 and UTC+5), but Tashkent moved out of the Soviet UTC+6 band after 1991, so the 1984 grouping is historically correct.
new_blocker_soviet_zones.consequence: Reversing the clock requires reversing post-Soviet time-zone reorganisation as well as the 1997 name changes. This was not in any previous blocker list.
new_blocker_soviet_zones.side_effect: It also RAISES confidence in Source 2: a careless transcription would be unlikely to reproduce a correct Soviet-era grouping.

plus30_notation.question: How are the half-hour zones written on the drum?
plus30_notation.answer: As a literal '+30' suffix on the place name: NEW DELHI +30, COLOMBO +30, RANGUN +30, KABUL +30.
plus30_notation.evidence: LOCAL VISUAL (UPLOAD-3/4), independently confirming the Tagesspiegel 2019 report of a '+ 30' inscription.
plus30_notation.grade: CONFIRMED for the modern drum; the 2019 profile attributes the practice to the original design, so probable but not locally verified for 1988-89.
plus30_notation.consequence: Any tape-reading procedure over the drum must decide what to do with these digits. K4 is 97 letters with no digits, so a reading that includes the half-hour faces must either skip the notation or transliterate it - a free choice, i.e. an extra degree of freedom that must be penalised.

north_south_band_rule.question: Is the upper/lower split within a face meaningful, or arbitrary?
north_south_band_rule.answer: Upper = northern places, lower = southern places, within each UTC sector.
north_south_band_rule.evidence: LOCAL VISUAL on four independent face pairs in UPLOAD-3/4 (KRASNOJARSK over HANOI/BANGKOK/PHNOM PENH/JAKARTA; IRKUTSK/ULAN-BATOR over PEKING..SINGAPUR; JAKUTSK over PJOENGJANG/TOKYO/SEOUL; CHABAROWSK/WLADIWOSTOK over SYDNEY/CANBERRA/MELBOURNE). Corroborates the Tagesspiegel account that the upper metal ring is the northern-hemisphere structural ring and the lower the southern.
north_south_band_rule.consequence: Band assignment is now PREDICTABLE from latitude rather than free. This removes the 2^k half of the per-face layout entropy and makes the upper/lower question answerable from a place list alone - a real reduction in the reconstruction problem, though the k! within-band ordering remains.

band_ordering.upper: Alphabetical, confirmed locally on the CET face (9/9).
band_ordering.lower: NOT alphabetical on the CET face. Reads roughly north-to-south with one inversion (ROM before BELGRAD).
band_ordering.grade: SUPPORTED for upper; the lower rule is UNRESOLVED - one face, one inversion, and I cannot exclude that the true rule is something else (installation convenience, name length) that merely correlates with latitude.
band_ordering.consequence: A single ordering rule does NOT govern both bands. Any reading procedure that assumes one does is wrong.

face_membership_moved.statement: NOWOSIBIRSK appears with KRASNOJARSK in 1984 (UPLOAD-2) and with OMSK/ALMATY/TASCHKENT in the modern frame (UPLOAD-3).
face_membership_moved.grade: LOCAL VISUAL on both ends. The sector assignment of a place CHANGED between 1984 and now.
face_membership_moved.consequence: Backward reversal from the modern list cannot assume a place stays on its face. Membership is per-era and must be read per-era. This is the strongest single argument against reconstructing 1988-89 from the modern list plus a change-log.

soviet_era_toponyms.consequence: At least five target-era names differ from the modern list, so the target-era letter multiset differs from the modern one. Confirms and extends new_blocker_soviet_zones: the blocker is real and is not limited to zone boundaries but reaches individual spellings.

face_97_observation.statement: My own reading of the CET/UTC+1 face gives 62 upper + 35 lower = 97 letters, the length of K4.
deflation: I did not predict 97 in advance.

There are 24 faces and at least 3 natural quantities per face (upper, lower, total), so ~72 values over a plausible 4-137 range: about 0.54 exact hits at 97 are expected by chance. One hit is unremarkable.
The count is fragile: drop LONDON (the one name the external transcription missed) and it is 91; add an unseen seventh lower line and it exceeds 97.
The face's date is DISPUTED, so this may not even be the target-era face.
face_97_observation.non_free_element: The one thing not chosen after the fact is WHICH face: it is the Berlin/CET face named by the BERLINCLOCK crib, and the face this programme was already targeting before the count was taken.
face_97_observation.grade: OBSERVATION, NOT EVIDENCE. It does not raise the Weltzeituhr hypothesis above PROMISING HYPOTHESIS and must not be used to motivate running EXP-024.

face_aliases._why: UPLOAD-1's adjacency was recorded with descriptive labels (read off face contents) because the hour ring cannot name a face. These labels denote the SAME physical faces as the sector-labelled nodes, and the CET upper/lower labels denote ONE face. Without this map the graph double-counts faces and reports more than 24.
